## Grammar

Basic word order is SVO; it has both prepositions and postpositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; noun before the numeral; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has a definite article before the noun, no indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, split alignment (ergative in some contexts, accusative in others), no grammatical number, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past and future; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs do not agree with their arguments.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; an inclusive/exclusive 'we' distinction; alienable and inalienable possession told apart; verb reduplication; a periphrastic causative; no passive; question words left in place; a decimal counting base.
Measured morphology: 3 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.3 (0 free word … 3 fused), 0 paradigm cells, 0 of them with allomorphy.
